requirement:
By default, authoring MUST suppress per-subject `true` judgment lines and show
each `false` judgment's subject and outcome on stderr, on both terminals and
redirected output. Existing progress counters and completion summaries MUST remain
available; FIXME notices and authoring errors MUST remain visible. Single-subject
authoring MUST retain its subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and
usage-record metadata.

`-v` and `--verbose` MUST additionally show each false judgment's recorded Markdown
rationale on stderr; rationales MUST be omitted by default. This applies to
single-subject and batch authoring. It MUST
NOT print true rationales or append recorded
input snapshots. Reporting MUST use the completed assessment's existing result,
without additional inference. In `--stdout` mode, stdout MUST remain only the
evidence JSON; verbose rationale and other diagnostics MUST go to stderr.
Verbosity MUST NOT change persistence, validation, or exit-status rules.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.invocation` {cite}`requirements.authoring.batch`
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.authoring.reporting`. I found no gap.

**Default reporting: false lines shown, true lines suppressed, on terminals and redirected output**
- Redirected batch: `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose]` runs without `-v`. It asserts that stderr has no `: true (usage:` lines and does have `requirements.alpha: false (usage:`. It also asserts that stderr has no ANSI escapes.
- Terminal batch: `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[terminal_progress_distinguishes_judgments_from_authoring_errors]` runs in a PTY. It asserts the same true/false line rules. It also asserts that the false rationale and the "Fixture judgment" text are absent by default.
- Single subject: `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]` asserts that stderr has `<SUBJECT>: false` and stdout does not. It also asserts that the rationale is absent by default.
- Single subject, true: `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` assert that no `<SUBJECT>: true` or `— true` line appears.

**Progress counters, completion summaries, FIXME notices, authoring errors remain**
- The PTY test asserts counted inspection progress, `6/6 finished`, active and queued counts, and elapsed time. It also asserts the final `true 3/false 1/FIXME 1/errors 1` counts and the stdout summary `5 authored; …; 1 failed`.
- The same PTY test asserts that `requirements.beta: FIXME` and `fixture model rejected` stay visible. The redirected batch test asserts both as well.
- The single-subject stdout-mode test asserts `— FIXME` on stderr for a FIXME judgment.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure]` asserts that the failing subject and its error text are reported.

**Single-subject metadata**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts the stdout header `<SUBJECT>: ollama / <MODEL>`, the `Evidence:` path and the `Usage:` line.
- The stdout-mode test asserts the subject/backend/model line, `Evidence: stdout`, and a usage path that is a real file.

**Verbose behavior**
- Rationale shown for false judgments only:
  - Batch: `batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose` toggles `--verbose` and asserts that `diagnostics.contains(rationale) == verbose`. The PTY test `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[verbose_false_rationale_is_readable_above_terminal_progress]` covers `-v` with terminal progress.
  - Single: `verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs` covers `-v` and `--verbose` with false, and `-v` with true. It asserts that the rationale appears if and only if the judgment is false.
- True rationales not printed: the batch test asserts that the gamma true rationale is absent. The single-subject test covers the true case.
- No input snapshots appended: the batch and PTY tests assert that `pub fn alpha()` is absent. The single-subject and stdout tests assert that `pub fn ready()`, the requirement text and the definition text are absent.
- No additional inference: the batch tests assert exactly 6 server requests in both modes. The single-subject tests assert `server.finish().len() == 1` after a verbose run.
- `--stdout` mode: `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` includes verbose false and true cases. It parses all of stdout as JSON, so any extra output would fail. It asserts that the rationale appears on stderr only for verbose false.
- Verbosity does not change persistence, validation or exit status:
  - The single-subject test compares the evidence determination and rationale, and runs `validate_repository` to check that errors match the determination.
  - The stdout test asserts that existing evidence is unchanged.
  - The batch tests assert a nonzero exit in both modes, with the same stdout summary.
  - The single-subject tests assert success in both modes.

A single-subject authoring error is asserted visible on stderr in other tests, for example the Bedrock options test and the cancel test. Those carry no `reporting` marker. This is at most a minor marking matter. The batch tests already cover the error-visibility obligation.

:::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} batch
`habeas author --all [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [-v|--verbose]` MUST author
the evidence of every current requirement and named example, together with the
reviews {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and
{cite}`requirements.references.site_review` include, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`.
`--all` MUST be mutually exclusive with a subject name and `--stdout`. It MUST
also delete each orphaned citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and each orphaned site review
under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and report each deletion; the
deletion MUST NOT require model configuration or credentials.
Failure to discover declarations or to read, scan, or parse project sources MUST report an error,
not a successful empty batch.
Each subject MUST receive an independent assessment with its own prompt, inputs,
judgment, and usage record. The command MUST report aggregate completion and each
authoring error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.reporting`, and retain
successful writes when another assessment fails. It MUST return a nonzero
exit status if any assessment fails. False judgments MUST still be written as
completed assessments; they remain failures under ordinary evidence validation.
A denied mandatory input MUST abort only the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`. Interruption MUST instead stop the
whole batch: queued assessments MUST NOT start, running assessments MUST be
cancelled, and an assessment whose evidence has not been written when the
interruption is observed MUST NOT begin committing it. After preparing a
temporary evidence file, the harness MUST check interruption again before its
atomic replacement; a replacement already in progress MAY finish. Evidence already written MUST be
retained, and the command MUST report the number of assessments not started as
a batch failure.
The bundled Habeas skills MUST direct the supervising agent to run this command
to create or refresh evidence. They MUST leave judgments, rationales, and input
snapshots to the authoring harness; the supervising agent addresses findings by
changing requirements, source citations, implementation, or tests.
